main_system_reason: The dock is the longest straight Harappan structure at Lothal and is drawn as excavated on the only measured plan of the whole town; the town plan's acropolis edges agree with it within a few degrees. The two excavation figures give local systems for the warehouse and for one house block, each relative to its own drawn rose.
notes: Rao's final report (1979) survives online only as a scan with its plates missing, so its general plan of the town is not available to us; we measured two of its text figures, the warehouse on the acropolis (Fig. 18) and Block B of the lower town (Fig. 17), and the colour site plan redrawn 'after Rao 1979' in Bisht's 2015 Dholavira report (Fig. 10.10 A). None of the three roses carries a letter or a statement of the kind of north. The three plans give different directions relative to their own roses: the warehouse blocks lie within about one degree of the cardinal directions, the dock and the acropolis platform of the town plan are turned a few degrees anticlockwise, and the walls of Block B about ten degrees anticlockwise. Each plan carries its own drawn rose, so these differences may come from the roses as much as from the buildings; the house walls of Block B are also short. The town plan is a small redrawing (871 x 690 px) in which most fortification is drawn as reconstructed; we measured only the dock and platform edges drawn as excavated, and the dock's short ends, which are not square to its long walls on that drawing, were not used. Warehouse block edges are short (three to eight metres) because each block is only a few metres across.
